newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Agrimoney should not change before 1999 -EU report.
newsitem.headline: Agrimoney should not change before 1999 -EU report.

text.p: European Union agrimonetary measures should not be reformed ahead of the planned move towards a single currency on January 1, 1999, the European Commission said in a report.

"No change should be made to the general way the present agri-monetary arrangements function pending their revision with a view to the third stage of economic and monetary union," said a report on the system's operation in 1995/96 (July/June).
But the Commission did call for simpler rules, urging farm ministers to approve a proposal to abolish green rates for import charges.
Green rates convert Ecu-based farm subsidies into national currencies.

Although future so-called appreciable revaluations of green rates should be implemented, distortions due to the freezing of green rates must not be aggravated because they would hinder the changeover to the euro, the repoort added.
An appreciable revaluation involves a greater reduction in common farm prices than increases from any previous devaluations.
Reforms introduced on February 1, 1995, abolished the costly switchover mechanism for protecting farmers in revaluing countries from lower prices.
But farmers will still be cushioned against income losses by a freezing of green rates for direct aid payments until January 1999. Compensatory aid is also be available on a decreasing scale.
